validator_exit_code_behaviour.citation: src/index.js, error() function (process.exit(1) on CLI-level validation failures) versus the run() function's try/finally block around renderMermaid(), which contains no catch clause or explicit non-zero exit for a rendering/parse failure
validator_exit_code_behaviour.rationale: mmdc DOES exit non-zero (via error()) for CLI usage mistakes: missing input file, missing config file, wrong output extension, missing output directory. It does NOT, in the retrieved code, appear to explicitly catch a Mermaid parse/render failure and translate it into a controlled non-zero exit — the try/finally only guarantees the browser is closed, not that a specific exit code is set on failure. Combined with the grammar-level finding in source-mermaid-erd-grammar.json that an undeclared-entity relationship is silently auto-vivified rather than rejected, the practical conclusion is: mmdc's exit-non-zero guarantee is reliable for CLI misuse and probably for hard syntax/lexer errors that throw inside renderMermaid() and go unhandled (Node's default behaviour is to exit 1 on an uncaught exception/unhandled rejection), but it has no deliberate, documented exit-code CONTRACT for malformed diagrams, and it has no semantic-validation layer at all, so a diagram that is syntactically valid but semantically inconsistent (e.g. references an undeclared entity) will not cause any non-zero exit — it renders 'successfully'. This is recorded as expressible-only-via-workaround (i.e., relying on undocumented default Node.js uncaught-exception behaviour) rather than not-expressible, because malformed input does appear to crash the process in practice per historical issue reports, but not as a designed, gated, documented contract the way the research question requires.

where_searched: web search across GitHub issues for mermaid-cli / mermaidjs/mermaid.cli
contrary_evidence_search.result: No dedicated 'validate' or 'lint' subcommand was found in mermaid-cli — only render-to-file (-o) with implicit validation as a side effect of attempting to render. No documented, stable exit-code CONTRACT for malformed or semantically inconsistent diagrams was found in the README or the retrieved source. A related historical issue on the predecessor repository ('mmdc process does not exit on error', mermaidjs/mermaid.cli issue #77) corroborates that this has been a known weak point in the tool's error handling, though that issue predates the current mermaid-js/mermaid-cli repository and is recorded here only as corroborating context, not as primary evidence for the current tool.
